A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 3DGUT work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and supplementary Sections A–F. Relocated material and renumbered figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction quality and rendering-speed results on four datasets, alongside kernel, projection-quality, and rendering demonstrations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds projection-sensitivity measurements and per-scene benchmark results.

M1.justification: The seven-point Unscented Transform, 3D particle evaluation, sorting, training losses, generalized Gaussian kernels, and hybrid rendering procedure remain unchanged. The added explanation of sigma-point counts does not alter the algorithm.

E1.justification: The four datasets and task families remain unchanged. Appendix C extends tested camera conditions through field-of-view sweeps, radial distortion coefficients from 0 to 0.5, and rolling-shutter translations from 0 to 0.35, beyond v1's selected camera/pose examples.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 1–5 and the EWA projection comparator are retained. The Waymo caption change from 3DGRT to ground truth corrects panels already labelled GT in v1 Figure 13; it does not replace a baseline.

E3.justification: New Figures 12–13 introduce parameter sweeps with mean/median KL summaries and specify the EWA Jacobians used for those comparisons. Existing benchmark preprocessing, 30k-iteration training, hardware, and the 500-sample Monte Carlo reference procedure remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds controlled sensitivity analyses testing projection accuracy as field of view, radial distortion, and rolling-shutter motion vary. These extend the existing fixed-configuration analysis, retained as Figure 14; the kernel quality/speed ablation is unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run variability, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new mean/median KL summaries measure projection error rather than experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: Tables 6–8 add per-scene results for Tanks & Temples, MipNeRF360, and ScanNet++. Figures 12–13 add sensitivity results, including UT median KL of 0.0044 at radial distortion k2=0 and 0.0043 at k2=0.5. All numerical entries in Tables 1–5 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 adds the assertion that 2N+1 sigma points match at least the first three moments of an N-dimensional target distribution. This is a limited mathematical characterization; Equations 1–16 and the backward-gradient derivation remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions claim support for complex cameras and rolling shutter through UT, efficient rasterization, and compatibility with secondary-ray tracing. The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same scientific scope.

C2.justification: Section 7 removes the claim that UT is faster than linearization and instead attributes overhead to UT and 3D particle evaluation. Appendix C qualifies the new comparisons by explaining that the standard EWA Jacobian does not account for radial distortion or rolling shutter.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit source-code availability statement and repository link, plus ScanNet++ scene identifiers in Table 8. The appendix's accompanying-video pointer is removed. Existing implementation, hyperparameter, and hardware disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: The same 57 cited works and positioning relative to 3DGS, 3DGRT, EWA, and earlier UT applications are retained. Bibliography relocation and citation back-reference changes do not alter research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract and secondary-ray explanation receive limited editing, the UT explanation expands, and Appendix F is renamed Additional Experimental Results. The supplement moves before the bibliography, while the main section sequence remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds two sensitivity-plot figures and three per-scene tables, reflows retained displays, adjusts Figure 8 labels, and renumbers subsequent appendix figures. It also corrects the Waymo caption while retaining the overall two-column design.

improvement.justification: The controlled sensitivity sweeps strengthen evidence for projection robustness, and per-scene tables make existing benchmark results easier to inspect. Added code-access information and corrections to the Waymo caption and runtime explanation improve reproducibility information and clarity. These are useful, limited gains; the method and aggregate benchmark findings remain stable.
